author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Ukraine is contracting for roughly 1,000 Patriot air-defense missiles with allied help and financing tied to a European Union loan, Defense Minister Yevhenii Khmara said.

Khmara told a meeting of the Ukraine Defense Contact Group that most of the missiles would arrive over several years. He asked partner countries to provide interceptors from existing stockpiles now, arguing that immediate defenses are needed against continuing Russian missile and drone attacks.

Germany separately said it would urgently supply additional Patriot PAC-2 interceptors from its own stocks and expand deliveries of other air-defense equipment. NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte urged members to increase support.

The contracts represent planned supply, not 1,000 missiles already delivered or available for use. Timing, participating suppliers and annual delivery volumes were not fully detailed in the initial report. Ukraine also identified a major financing gap for drone purchases. The story remains developing because allied commitments, production schedules and near-term transfers will determine how quickly the announced plan strengthens air defenses.
dek: Kyiv’s defense chief says most deliveries will take years and is asking allies to release interceptors from existing stocks sooner.
headline: Ukraine contracts for about 1,000 Patriot missiles
